intro.title: Build typed registry with key constraints
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a typed registry that stores and retrieves values using specific keys, ensuring type safety throughout. You will learn how to use TypeScript's generic types and key constraints to define which keys are allowed in the registry. The main technologies involved are TypeScript interfaces, generics, and union types for restricting keys. By the end, you'll have a functional registry that prevents invalid keys at compile time, reinforcing type-safe data structures.
intro.usecase: A typed registry with key constraints is a foundational pattern for managing dynamic, type-safe collections in real-world applications. For example, in a dashboard builder, you might have a registry of available widgets (like charts, tables, or metrics) where each widget type is registered under a unique key, ensuring that only valid, pre-defined components can be instantiated. This pattern is also essential in plugin systems, such as a code editor's extension marketplace, where extensions must be registered with specific identifiers to prevent conflicts and enable safe, predictable loading. By enforcing these constraints, developers can build scalable, maintainable systems that prevent runtime errors and improve developer experience.
